info.title: Document360 Customer API
info.description:
Document360 RESTful APIs let you integrate your documentation with your software — onboard readers, manage articles, automate publishing, and more.

Full reference: [API Documentation](https://apidocs.document360.io/docs).

## Authentication
V3 authenticates with an **API key** — not the `api_token` used by V1/V2. Create one in the Document360 portal under **Settings → Knowledge base portal → API keys**, then click **Create API key**. (Projects that still have the older screen show two tabs; choose **Enhanced keys (v3)**, or pick **API v3** from the Create menu.)

Send it in the `X-API-Key` header:

```
X-API-Key: d360_sk_...
```

The plaintext key is shown **once**, at creation — only its hash is stored, so a lost key must be replaced rather than recovered. Each key carries a fixed portal role, content role and content-access scope, supports an optional expiry, and can be disabled or deleted at any time from the same screen. Treat it as an opaque string: it is a pre-shared secret, not an OAuth 2.0 access token, and must not be parsed.

For flows that act on behalf of a specific person, V3 also accepts an OAuth 2.0 bearer token carrying the `customerApi` scope.

API access is part of your subscription plan. If your plan does not include it, every endpoint returns `403` with the error code `FEATURE_NOT_IN_LICENSE` — including for keys created while an earlier plan was active. Contact your Customer Success Manager or `support@document360.com` to enable it.

> **Note on terminology:** V1/V2 call these *API tokens* and manage them under **Settings → Knowledge base portal → API tokens**. V3 keys are a separate credential with their own screen, roles and scope — a V1/V2 token will not authenticate a V3 request.

## Rate Limits
All endpoints are rate-limited per API key per project. Default limits vary by plan. When rate-limited, responses include `Retry-After`, `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` headers. Use exponential backoff with jitter for optimal retry behavior.

get.description:
Returns a list of articles ranked by how often they are cited as sources in AI-generated
answers. Use this to understand which articles are most relied upon by the AI search
engine. This endpoint returns all matching articles and does not support pagination.
Requires `ViewAnalytics` permission.

answered and unanswered counts, conversation count, and user feedback (likes/dislikes).

Use this endpoint to build AI search dashboard tiles. Requires `ViewAnalytics` permission.

get.description:
Returns AI-identified topic clusters from search queries, ranked by question count.
Topics with `is_no_search_cluster` set to `true` represent clusters of
unanswered queries — these highlight content gaps. Use this endpoint to discover
emerging user interests and unmet content needs. This endpoint returns all matching
topics and does not support pagination. Requires `ViewAnalytics` permission.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of style-guide summaries for the supplied language. The body
(`content`) is omitted from list responses to keep payloads small — call
`GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/ai/writer-style-guides/{styleGuideId}` for the full body.
Style guides are scoped per language; the same author voice expressed in a different
language exists as a separate record with its own `id`.

parameters.name: search_text
parameters.description: Optional case-insensitive substring filter on style-guide name.

parameters.name: include_total_count
parameters.description: Set to `true` to include `total_count` in the response.

post.description: Runs the import inline and returns its outcome, exactly as it did before WI 340551. Why this endpoint still exists and still behaves this way. WI 340551 changed it in place to return `202` and process on a worker. That was a breaking change to a route with live production traffic — 15 projects across prod-eu, prod-us and prod-wk — so it was reverted. The background behaviour now lives at its own route and this one is unchanged for the callers that already depend on it. It is published as deprecated, not hidden. An earlier revision removed it from the spec so that no new integration would adopt it. That was reversed: the CLI builds its whole command tree from this specification and rebuilds it nightly, so hiding the route deletes `d360 apiref import` from the next release — taking the command away from the very callers the revert exists to protect, and giving them an unknown-command error instead of a warning. Deprecated-and-visible keeps the command, marks it in the docs, and still steers new work away. Use `POST /v3/projects/{projectId}/api-references/imports` instead. It answers `202` immediately with an `Operation-Location` header and runs the parse on a worker. This route imports inside the request, so it stays subject to the ingress timeout and to the memory pressure the worker exists to remove — a large specification is the case that fails here and succeeds there. It is not scheduled for removal until the known callers have migrated. The non-async improvements from WI 340551 are kept, because they were never part of the breaking change: multipart `file` upload, `422` carrying the parser's own errors and warnings, the API-documentation access gate, and requiring `user_id` when `publish_articles` is set.

Defaults to `false` (WI 340551): the caller is told what the import would do and re-submits with `force_import: true` to go ahead. This default changed. It was `true`, matching the V1/V2 `ForceImport` contract. Under `true` a resync deleted endpoints and said nothing about it, because the deletion report was computed only on the strict path — so on V3, where this initialised to `true`, a destructive resync was always silent. The gate is broader than deletions. Under `false` the request is refused if the spec yields ANY error or warning, or if `servers` is absent, so a spec that parses perfectly can still be refused. That is the cost of the change and it is deliberate: a refusal is recoverable in one call, a silent deletion is not.

post.description: Re-runs the import pipeline against the existing API reference record, replacing its spec source. The diff is reflected as updates to the auto-generated articles — additions, modifications, and removals of operations all flow through. Use this after the underlying API has shipped a new version of its OpenAPI/Swagger spec. The workspace is inferred from the existing API reference, so it does not need to be supplied. Returns `404` if the API reference does not exist or belongs to a different project. Supply the refreshed spec through exactly ONE of three sources: `url` — a publicly reachable specification URL (`application/json` body).`file` — the specification uploaded directly. Preferred for a local spec; requires the request to be sent as `multipart/form-data`, with the spec under the form field `file` and the remaining fields as form fields (`publish_articles`, `force_import`).`content` — deprecated, use `file` instead. The raw spec as a JSON string. Still fully supported and not scheduled for removal. The resync runs in the background. This endpoint ACCEPTS the work and returns `202 Accepted` immediately. The response body carries `operation_id` and `operation_status: "queued"`, and the `Operation-Location` response header holds the URL to poll. Track it with `GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/operations/{operationId}` until its status is terminal; the resync's outcome — parser findings, and `deleted_endpoints` when the new spec drops operations — arrives in that operation's `result`. The API reference itself is still resolved BEFORE the work is accepted, so an unknown or foreign `apiReferenceId` is a `404` here rather than a queued job that fails later. One job per project. A project may have only one import or resync open at a time. A second, different request while one is open is refused with `409 Conflict` naming the operation to poll; re-submitting an IDENTICAL request returns the operation already running. Polling needs a different permission from starting. This action requires `articles.update`, a CONTENT role permission, while `GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/operations/{operationId}` requires `projectSettings.view`, a PORTAL role permission. Neither implies the other, so a token that can start a resync may receive an `Operation-Location` it cannot read. Grant both to any integration that resyncs and then polls. See the import action for why this belongs to the shared operations endpoint rather than to this route.

A second, different request while one is open is refused with `409 Conflict` naming the operation to poll. Re-submitting an IDENTICAL request is not a conflict — it returns the operation already running rather than starting a second one. Polling needs a different permission from starting. This action requires `articles.update`, a CONTENT role permission, while `GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/operations/{operationId}` requires `projectSettings.view`, a PORTAL role permission. They are separate families and neither implies the other, so a token that can start an import may receive an `Operation-Location` it cannot read. Grant both to any integration that imports and then polls. This is a property of the shared operations endpoint rather than of this action: `POST /v3/projects/{projectId}/categories/{categoryId}/archive` has the same split (`categories.delete` to start, `projectSettings.view` to poll) and predates this route.

get.description:
Returns the comment threads on an article in a single resolution status (defaults to `open`),
newest first. Each comment's `id` matches the `data-comment-id` attribute of its marker in
the content returned by `GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/articles/{articleId}?content_mode=raw`, so a
consumer editing the content can re-associate a thread with the exact text it annotates. Use
`commented_text` to read the annotated text directly, without searching the content yourself.
            
The list is cursor-paginated by modification time: pass the response's `next_cursor` back as
`cursor` to fetch the next (older) page. `total_count` is populated on the first page only.
            
**Access:** requires the `articles.update` permission, passes the same node-level ACL as the
article itself, and requires a resolvable user identity — a machine-to-machine token with no acting
user is rejected with `422`.

### Related endpoints

**Next**
- `POST /v3/projects/{project_id}/articles/{article_id}/comments` — Starts a new thread on this article.
- `PATCH /v3/projects/{project_id}/articles/{article_id}/comments/{comment_id}` — Resolves, reopens, or edits one of the threads returned here.

**See also**
- `GET /v3/projects/{project_id}/articles/{article_id}` — Reads the article content the comment markers live in. Each comment's `id` is the `data-comment-id` of its marker, so fetch with `content_mode=raw` to line them up.

post.summary: Add a comment to an article.
post.description:
Creates a new comment thread on an article's content.
            
**This is the second of two calls.** The marker must already be in the content — update it first via
`PATCH /v3/projects/{projectId}/articles/{articleId}`, then create the thread here with the same
`comment_id`. The full procedure, and why the order matters, is described below.
            
The comment id is supplied by the caller because it is the same value written into the marker, which
also makes a retried request safe: repeating it returns `409` rather than creating a second
thread. Every comment this endpoint creates is text-anchored, so the marker check always applies —
there is no scope that skips it. The thread is created against the article's latest version in the
requested language.
            
**Access:** requires the `articles.update` permission, passes the same node-level ACL as the
article itself, and requires a resolvable user identity — a machine-to-machine token with no acting
user is rejected with `422`. Authorship is taken from the authenticated identity, never from the
request body.

### Related endpoints

**Next**
- `POST /v3/projects/{project_id}/articles/{article_id}/comments/{comment_id}/replies` — Replies to the thread just created.
- `PATCH /v3/projects/{project_id}/articles/{article_id}/comments/{comment_id}` — Resolves the thread once the discussion is settled.

### This is step 2 of 2 — the marker must already be in the content

Call `PATCH /v3/projects/{project_id}/articles/{article_id}` first to put the marker in the content, then this endpoint to create the thread.

A comment is **two facts that must agree**: a marker in the content that highlights the annotated text, and
the comment thread itself. Two endpoints write them, and both calls must carry the **same `comment_id`**.

1. **Add the marker** — `PATCH /v3/projects/{project_id}/articles/{article_id}`
   Send the content with the annotated text wrapped in an element carrying `data-comment-id="<comment_id>"`.
   Generate the id yourself (a GUID) — you reuse it in step 2.
2. **Create the thread** — `POST /v3/projects/{project_id}/articles/{article_id}/comments`
   Send that same value as `comment_id` in the body.

**Order matters.** Step 2 checks the marker is present and returns `422` if it is not, so a thread can never
exist without the text it annotates. The reverse is not enforced: a marker with no thread is an inert
highlight, so if step 2 fails, either retry it or take the marker back out.

The request examples on both operations use the same `comment_id` (`b7f3c1a0-5e42-4d18-9a6c-2f8091d3e547`) and
the same annotated text (`single sign-on`), so you can copy step 1, then step 2, and
the pair works unchanged.

Comments are supported only on block-editor (Editor 3.0) content; any other editor is rejected with `422`.

post.description:
Adds a reply to an existing comment thread. A reply annotates nothing in the content, so no marker and
no content update are involved — this is a single call.
            
**A resolved thread cannot be replied to** — that returns `409`, distinct from a payload error, so
a client can tell "reopen the thread first" from "fix your request". Reply creation is create-only: a
`reply_id` that already exists returns `409` rather than overwriting the existing reply. The
per-thread reply limit is enforced here.
            
**Access:** requires the `articles.update` permission, the same node-level ACL as the article, and
a resolvable user identity. Authorship comes from the authenticated identity.

### Related endpoints

**Before you call this**
- `GET /v3/projects/{project_id}/articles/{article_id}/comments` — Lists the threads on the article. Supplies the `comment_id` to reply to, and shows whether the thread is resolved — a resolved thread rejects replies with `409`.

**See also**
- `PATCH /v3/projects/{project_id}/articles/{article_id}/comments/{comment_id}` — Reopens a resolved thread so it can be replied to again.

patch.summary: Resolve, reopen, or edit a comment on an article.
patch.description:
Updates an existing thread. Send `status` to resolve or reopen it, `comment` to replace its
body, or both in one call. Omitted fields are left untouched.
            
**Resolving is idempotent.** Sending the same `status` twice is accepted and writes nothing the
second time, so a client that retries after a timeout cannot flip the thread back. A transition that
cannot be reached is refused with `422` rather than silently applied as something else: a thread
becomes `reopened` only after having been `resolved`, and `open` cannot be set at all.
            
**The two fields have different access rules**, which is why one call can succeed for one and fail for
the other:
<list type="bullet"><item>`status` — requires permission to resolve comments on this article. Any permitted user can
resolve someone else's thread.</item><item>`comment` — restricted to the thread's **original author**, whatever their permissions.
Anyone else should reply instead, and receives `403`.</item></list>
            
Replies are not edited here — see
`POST /v3/projects/{projectId}/articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId}/replies` to add one.

### Related endpoints

**Before you call this**
- `GET /v3/projects/{project_id}/articles/{article_id}/comments` — Lists the threads on the article. Supplies the `comment_id` to update, and the current `status` — which determines whether `resolved` or `reopened` is reachable.

**See also**
- `POST /v3/projects/{project_id}/articles/{article_id}/comments/{comment_id}/replies` — Adds a reply. Editing the body here is restricted to the thread's author; anyone else should reply instead.

requestBody.description: The status and/or body to apply.

Resolve the thread.summary: Marks the discussion settled. Safe to repeat: a thread that is already resolved is left alone and still returns 200, so a retry after a timeout cannot reopen it.

Reopen a resolved thread.summary: Returns a resolved thread to discussion. Only reachable from `resolved` — reopening a thread that was never resolved is rejected with 422, and `open` cannot be set at all.

Edit the comment body (author only).summary: Replaces the body and its @-mentions. Restricted to the thread's original author whatever their permissions; anyone else gets 403 and should reply instead.

get.description:
Returns the latest version of the article (draft or published). To retrieve a specific version,
use `GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/articles/{articleId}/versions/{versionNumber}` instead.
The response includes both raw content and rendered HTML.
For private or mixed-visibility projects, SAS tokens are appended to media URLs in the content by default.

parameters.name: content_mode
parameters.description:
Controls how content is processed in the response. Defaults to `raw`.

**raw** — Returns content as stored in the knowledge base. Snippets, Variables, and Glossary terms remain as their placeholder tokens (e.g., `{{snippet:intro}}`, `{{variable:productName}}`). SAS tokens are appended to media URLs for private/mixed-visibility projects. Internal notes are preserved.
*Use when:* building an authoring UI, running a GET-then-PUT round trip to edit an article, migrating content between projects, diffing two versions, or syncing source-of-truth content to an external system.

**display** — Returns fully rendered content ready for end-user consumption. Snippets, Variables, and Glossary terms are resolved inline into HTML, SAS tokens are appended to media URLs, and internal notes are removed.
*Use when:* rendering articles on a public site, in-app reader, chatbot answer, email digest, or any read-only surface where the reader should never see unresolved placeholders or internal notes.

**Warning:** never feed `display` output back into a create/update call. Snippet, Variable, and Glossary references are expanded into literal inline HTML, so saving the response as new content destroys the links to those reusable components in your source article.

patch.description:
Partial update — only fields included in the request body are modified; omitted fields remain unchanged.
            
**Reorder within the same category:** send `order` (0-based position among sibling articles;
lower numbers appear higher in the list).
            
**Move to a different category:** send `category_id` (the destination category's id),
optionally with `order` to position it there. Combine both to move and position in one request.
            
**Content and title updates:** `content` and `title` are both stored on the article version,
so neither can be changed on a published version without creating a draft first. When `auto_fork`
is true and the target version is published, a new draft version is automatically created and the
update is applied to the draft. If `auto_fork` is false (default), the request returns a 422
error. Fields that are not version-scoped — `order`, `category_id`, `hidden`,
`translation_option` — apply to the article itself and never require a fork.
            
When authenticating with an API key or API token, send `user_id` together with
`auto_fork: true`; it identifies the author of the new draft. OAuth user tokens don't need it.

### Related endpoints

**Next**
- `POST /v3/projects/{project_id}/articles/{article_id}/publish` — Publishes the edit. Content changes stay in the draft until the article is published.

**See also**
- `GET /v3/projects/{project_id}/articles/{article_id}` — Reads the article back. Use `content_mode=raw` to see the stored source rather than the rendered form.

### Adding a comment starts here (step 1 of 2)

This endpoint writes the content. It is also **step 1 of adding a comment** — see
`POST /v3/projects/{project_id}/articles/{article_id}/comments` for step 2.

A comment is **two facts that must agree**: a marker in the content that highlights the annotated text, and
the comment thread itself. Two endpoints write them, and both calls must carry the **same `comment_id`**.

1. **Add the marker** — `PATCH /v3/projects/{project_id}/articles/{article_id}`
   Send the content with the annotated text wrapped in an element carrying `data-comment-id="<comment_id>"`.
   Generate the id yourself (a GUID) — you reuse it in step 2.
2. **Create the thread** — `POST /v3/projects/{project_id}/articles/{article_id}/comments`
   Send that same value as `comment_id` in the body.

**Order matters.** Step 2 checks the marker is present and returns `422` if it is not, so a thread can never
exist without the text it annotates. The reverse is not enforced: a marker with no thread is an inert
highlight, so if step 2 fails, either retry it or take the marker back out.

The request examples on both operations use the same `comment_id` (`b7f3c1a0-5e42-4d18-9a6c-2f8091d3e547`) and
the same annotated text (`single sign-on`), so you can copy step 1, then step 2, and
the pair works unchanged.

Comments are supported only on block-editor (Editor 3.0) content; any other editor is rejected with `422`.

Update title and content with auto-fork.summary: Updates the article title and content. When auto_fork is true and the target version is published, a new draft version is created automatically, authored by user_id. user_id is required with auto_fork when using an API key; it is ignored for OAuth user tokens.

# Introduction
This updated guide walks you through configuring SSO for your organization.

Step 1 of 2 — add a comment marker to th.summary:
Adding a comment takes **two calls**, and this is the first: put the marker in the content, then create the thread with `POST /v3/projects/{projectId}/articles/{articleId}/comments` using the *Step 2 of 2* example there. Both examples use the same `comment_id` (`b7f3c1a0-5e42-4d18-9a6c-2f8091d3e547`), so you can send this body and then that one unchanged.

Wrap the annotated text in an element carrying `data-comment-id="<comment_id>"`, where the id is a GUID you generate. The id is repeated in `class` because that is what Editor 3.0 emits and what it styles the highlight from.

**Comments are supported only on block-editor articles** — a markdown or wysiwyg article stores the marker but renders it as an inert highlight with no discussion attached, so the create endpoint rejects those with `422`. This step is never optional: every comment this API creates is text-anchored, so the marker check always applies.

Reorder an article within its category.summary: Moves the article to position 0 (top) among the other articles in its category, without changing content or category.

Move article to a different category.summary: Moves the article to a new category and positions it there. Combine category_id with order to move and reorder in one request.

Update a specific version.summary: Targets a specific draft version for the update. Use version_number to specify which version to update.

get.description:
Retrieves the content for a specific historical version of the article. Use `GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/articles/{articleId}/versions`
to list available version numbers. For private or mixed-visibility projects, SAS tokens are appended to media URLs in the content by default.
Returns `404` if the article or version number does not exist.

parameters.name: content_mode
parameters.description:
Controls how content is processed in the response. Defaults to `raw`.

**raw** — Returns content as stored in the knowledge base. Snippets, Variables, and Glossary terms remain as their placeholder tokens (e.g., `{{snippet:intro}}`, `{{variable:productName}}`). SAS tokens are appended to media URLs for private/mixed-visibility projects. Internal notes are preserved.
*Use when:* building an authoring UI, running a GET-then-PUT round trip to edit an article, migrating content between projects, diffing two versions, or syncing source-of-truth content to an external system.

**display** — Returns fully rendered content ready for end-user consumption. Snippets, Variables, and Glossary terms are resolved inline into HTML, SAS tokens are appended to media URLs, and internal notes are removed.
*Use when:* rendering articles on a public site, in-app reader, chatbot answer, email digest, or any read-only surface where the reader should never see unresolved placeholders or internal notes.

**Warning:** never feed `display` output back into a create/update call. Snippet, Variable, and Glossary references are expanded into literal inline HTML, so saving the response as new content destroys the links to those reusable components in your source article.

post.description:
Creates a new article in draft status. The `workspace_id` field is required and determines
which workspace the article belongs to. If `category_id` is omitted, the article
is placed in the root of the workspace. The `content_type` defaults to Markdown (0) if not specified.
After creation, use the publish endpoint to make the article visible to readers.

### Related endpoints

**Before you call this**
- `GET /v3/projects/{project_id}/workspaces` — Lists the project's workspaces. Supplies the required `workspace_id`.
- `GET /v3/projects/{project_id}/workspaces/{workspace_id}/categories` — Lists the category tree of a workspace. Supplies the required `category_id` — an article is always created inside a category.
- `GET /v3/projects/{project_id}/users` — Lists team accounts. Supplies `user_id`, which is required when authenticating with a machine-to-machine token and no `X-Acting-User-Id` header.

**Next**
- `PATCH /v3/projects/{project_id}/articles/{article_id}` — Sets the article's title, content, order or category after creation.
- `POST /v3/projects/{project_id}/articles/{article_id}/publish` — Publishes the draft. A newly created article is a draft and is not visible to readers until this is called.

Create a Markdown article.summary: Creates a new article with Markdown content in a specific category. The article is created in draft status.

Creates a new draft version copied from an existing version, so edits can be made
without affecting the live published version. The request body is optional: when omitted
(or when `version_number` is null), the currently published version is forked.
Provide `version_number` to fork a specific historical version instead — list available
version numbers from `GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/articles/{articleId}/versions`.
If the article has no published version and no `version_number` is given, a 422 error is returned.
Alternatively, set `auto_fork` to true on the update endpoint to fork automatically when needed.

patch.description:
Performs partial updates on multiple articles in a single request. Each article update is
independent; if one fails, the others are still applied. Only fields included in each item
are modified; omitted fields remain unchanged. Maximum 100 articles per request.
            
**Per-item results:** the response is always `200` with one result per item; check each item's
`success` flag. Items are applied in order and committed individually, so a failure part-way
through does not roll back the items that already succeeded.
            
**Content and title updates:** `auto_fork` is honoured per item and behaves exactly as it does
on `PATCH /articles/{articleId}` — `content` and `title` are version-scoped, so
changing either on a published version requires `auto_fork: true` (which creates the draft and
applies the update there). Without it, that item fails while the rest of the batch proceeds.
            
When authenticating with an API key or API token, send `user_id` together with
`auto_fork: true`; it identifies the author of the new draft. OAuth user tokens don't need it.
A missing or unknown `user_id` is reported as one `422` that names each failing item
(for example `articles[0].user_id`), before any item is written.

requestBody.description: Bulk update details. Maximum 100 articles per request.

Bulk update two articles.summary: Updates multiple articles in a single request. Each item must include the article_id. Maximum 100 articles per request. auto_fork is per item: the first article changes its title, which is version-scoped, so it forks a draft, authored by that item's user_id, rather than rewriting the published version. The second changes only visibility, needs no fork, and so needs no user_id.

patch.description:
Partial update — only fields present in the request body are modified.
            
**Reorder within the same parent:** send `order` (0-based position among its siblings;
lower numbers appear higher in the navigation). Sibling categories are re-indexed automatically.
            
**Move to a different parent:** send `parent_category_id` (the new parent's id), optionally
with `order` to set its position in the new parent. Send `parent_category_id` as an
empty string to move the category to the workspace root. Combine both fields in one call to move
and position in a single request.
            
**Hide from readers:** send `hidden`. Visibility is per-language and this endpoint targets the
workspace's default language; the category's articles and sub-categories inherit the hidden state.
Hiding affects the knowledge base site only — the category stays visible and editable in the portal.
Changing visibility additionally requires the *publish* content permission — it changes what readers
see, exactly as publishing does — so a caller carrying only the update-categories permission is
refused with a `403`. This applies to every permission-scoped credential: a user token, an M2M
token with `X-Acting-User-Id`, and a scoped API key. A legacy anonymous M2M token is not
permission-scoped and is unaffected.
            
The response carries the category as persisted, re-read after the write, so every field you sent can
be verified from it without a follow-up `GET`.
            
This endpoint does not update body content or settings; use
`PATCH /v3/projects/{projectId}/categories/{categoryId}/content` and
`PATCH /v3/projects/{projectId}/categories/{categoryId}/settings` respectively for those.

Reorder a category within its parent.summary: Moves the category to position 0 (top) among its siblings. Other siblings are re-indexed automatically.

Move a category under a different parent.summary: Moves the category beneath a new parent category and places it at position 2 there. Send parent_category_id as an empty string to move it to the workspace root.

Rename and reorder a category.summary: Updates the category's name, sort order, and icon in one request.

Hide a category from readers.summary: Hides the category on the knowledge base site for the workspace's default language. Its articles and sub-categories inherit the hidden state; the portal is unaffected. Send hidden as false to make it visible again. The response reports the stored value, so no follow-up GET is needed to confirm it applied.

Retrieves the markdown or HTML body content of a category.
For private or mixed-visibility projects, SAS tokens are appended to media URLs in the content by default.
When `contentMode` is set to `display`, Snippets, Variables, and Glossaries are resolved inline.

parameters.name: content_mode
parameters.description:
Controls how content is processed in the response. Defaults to `raw`.

**raw** — Returns content as stored in the knowledge base. Snippets, Variables, and Glossary terms remain as their placeholder tokens (e.g., `{{snippet:intro}}`, `{{variable:productName}}`). SAS tokens are appended to media URLs for private/mixed-visibility projects. Internal notes are preserved.
*Use when:* building an authoring UI, running a GET-then-PUT round trip to edit an article, migrating content between projects, diffing two versions, or syncing source-of-truth content to an external system.

**display** — Returns fully rendered content ready for end-user consumption. Snippets, Variables, and Glossary terms are resolved inline into HTML, SAS tokens are appended to media URLs, and internal notes are removed.
*Use when:* rendering articles on a public site, in-app reader, chatbot answer, email digest, or any read-only surface where the reader should never see unresolved placeholders or internal notes.

**Warning:** never feed `display` output back into a create/update call. Snippet, Variable, and Glossary references are expanded into literal inline HTML, so saving the response as new content destroys the links to those reusable components in your source article.

patch.description:
Updates the body content of the latest draft version. If `auto_fork` is `true` and no draft exists,
a new draft is automatically forked from the published version before applying the update. The `updated_by`
field is required when using an M2M token. SAS tokens in media URLs are automatically stripped before
persisting. Use `GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/categories/{categoryId}/content` with `raw` mode to
retrieve content suitable for round-trip editing.

### Related endpoints

**Next**
- `POST /v3/projects/{project_id}/categories/{category_id}/publish` — Publishes the edit.

**See also**
- `GET /v3/projects/{project_id}/categories/{category_id}/content` — Reads the page content back.

### Adding a comment starts here (step 1 of 2)

This endpoint writes the content. It is also **step 1 of adding a comment** — see
`POST /v3/projects/{project_id}/categories/{category_id}/comments` for step 2.

A comment is **two facts that must agree**: a marker in the content that highlights the annotated text, and
the comment thread itself. Two endpoints write them, and both calls must carry the **same `comment_id`**.

1. **Add the marker** — `PATCH /v3/projects/{project_id}/categories/{category_id}/content`
   Send the content with the annotated text wrapped in an element carrying `data-comment-id="<comment_id>"`.
   Generate the id yourself (a GUID) — you reuse it in step 2.
2. **Create the thread** — `POST /v3/projects/{project_id}/categories/{category_id}/comments`
   Send that same value as `comment_id` in the body.

**Order matters.** Step 2 checks the marker is present and returns `422` if it is not, so a thread can never
exist without the text it annotates. The reverse is not enforced: a marker with no thread is an inert
highlight, so if step 2 fails, either retry it or take the marker back out.

The request examples on both operations use the same `comment_id` (`b7f3c1a0-5e42-4d18-9a6c-2f8091d3e547`) and
the same annotated text (`single sign-on`), so you can copy step 1, then step 2, and
the pair works unchanged.

Comments are supported only on block-editor (Editor 3.0) content; any other editor is rejected with `422`.

post.description:
Creates a new category within the specified workspace. Requires `UpdateCategories` permission.
The `user_id` field is required when using an M2M (machine-to-machine) token rather than a user token.
Supports `Markdown`, `WYSIWYG`, and `Block` content types. If `slug` is omitted it is
auto-generated from the category name; duplicate slugs will cause a `422` validation error.
            
Send `hidden` as `true` to create the category already hidden from readers, so an internal
or system category is never reader-facing between creation and a follow-up update. It applies to
every language in the workspace.

### Related endpoints

**Before you call this**
- `GET /v3/projects/{project_id}/workspaces` — Lists the project's workspaces. Supplies the required `workspace_id`.
- `GET /v3/projects/{project_id}/workspaces/{workspace_id}/categories` — Lists the category tree. Supplies `parent_category_id` when nesting under an existing category.
- `GET /v3/projects/{project_id}/users` — Lists team accounts. Supplies `user_id` for machine-to-machine tokens.

**Next**
- `PATCH /v3/projects/{project_id}/categories/{category_id}/content` — Sets the page content. Only page categories carry content; folder and index categories have none.
- `POST /v3/projects/{project_id}/categories/{category_id}/publish` — Publishes the category so readers can see it.

Create a top-level category.summary: Creates a new folder-type category at the root level of a workspace.

Create a nested category with content.summary: Creates a page-type category nested under an existing parent category.

post.description:
Archives the specified language version: the category becomes read-only (every other write
action on this language answers `409` until it is restored) and is excluded from
publish/search surfaces. A leaf category (no children) archives synchronously and returns
`200`. A category with any children (article or category) instead cascades — every
descendant is archived before the category itself — and, since a synchronous request cannot
bound how long a deep cascade takes, is dispatched to a background operation: the response is
`202` with an `Operation-Location` header; poll
`GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/operations/{operationId}` for completion. Requires
`DeleteCategories` permission — archive is a deletion-class action, and this is the same
ACL the Portal's Archive action uses.

post.description:
Creates a new draft version copied from an existing version of the category. The request body is
optional: when omitted (or when `version_number` is null), the currently published version is forked.
Provide `version_number` to fork a specific historical version instead — list available version
numbers from `GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/categories/{categoryId}/versions`. If the category has
no published version and no `version_number` is given, a 422 error is returned. Returns `409 Conflict`
if a draft version already exists for this category. The newly created draft can then be edited via
`PATCH /v3/projects/{projectId}/categories/{categoryId}/content`. The response includes the full content
of the new draft version.

requestBody.description: Optional fork options. When omitted, the currently published version is forked.

Fork the currently published version (de.summary: Omit the body entirely, or send an empty object. The currently published version is forked into a new draft.

patch.description:
Batch-updates content for multiple categories in a single request. Each item is processed sequentially and
the response contains per-item `success` results. Supports `auto_fork` per item to automatically
create a draft if none exists. Use `PATCH /v3/projects/{projectId}/categories/{categoryId}/content` for
single-category updates with more detailed error information.
            
When authenticating with an API key or API token, send `updated_by` on every item that sets
`auto_fork: true`; it identifies the author of the new draft. OAuth user tokens don't need it.
A missing or unknown `updated_by` is reported as one `422` that names each failing item
(for example `categories[0].updated_by`), before any item is written.

post.summary: Add a comment to a page category.
post.description: Creates a new comment thread on a page category's content. Only page categories carry content; folder and index categories return `404`. **This is the second of two calls.** The marker must already be in the content — update it first via `PATCH /v3/projects/{projectId}/categories/{categoryId}/content`, then create the thread here with the same `comment_id`. The full procedure, and why the order matters, is described below. Semantics otherwise match the article endpoint: the caller supplies the id, a repeat returns `409`, and the marker check always applies — every comment this endpoint creates is text-anchored, so there is no scope that skips it. **Access:** requires the `categories.update` permission, passes the same node-level ACL as the category itself, and requires a resolvable user identity. Authorship is taken from the authenticated identity, never from the request body. ### Related endpoints **Next** - `POST /v3/projects/{project_id}/categories/{category_id}/comments/{comment_id}/replies` — Replies to the thread just created. - `PATCH /v3/projects/{project_id}/categories/{category_id}/comments/{comment_id}` — Resolves the thread once the discussion is settled. ### This is step 2 of 2 — the marker must already be in the content Call `PATCH /v3/projects/{project_id}/categories/{category_id}/content` first to put the marker in the content, then this endpoint to create the thread. A comment is **two facts that must agree**: a marker in the content that highlights the annotated text, and the comment thread itself. Two endpoints write them, and both calls must carry the **same `comment_id`**. 1. **Add the marker** — `PATCH /v3/projects/{project_id}/categories/{category_id}/content` Send the content with the annotated text wrapped in an element carrying `data-comment-id=""`. Generate the id yourself (a GUID) — you reuse it in step 2. 2. **Create the thread** — `POST /v3/projects/{project_id}/categories/{category_id}/comments` Send that same value as `comment_id` in the body. **Order matters.** Step 2 checks the marker is present and returns `422` if it is not, so a thread can never exist without the text it annotates. The reverse is not enforced: a marker with no thread is an inert highlight, so if step 2 fails, either retry it or take the marker back out. The request examples on both operations use the same `comment_id` (`b7f3c1a0-5e42-4d18-9a6c-2f8091d3e547`) and the same annotated text (`single sign-on`), so you can copy step 1, then step 2, and the pair works unchanged. Comments are supported only on block-editor (Editor 3.0) content; any other editor is rejected with `422`.

Step 2 of 2 — create the comment thread.summary:
The second of the two calls that add a comment. It pairs with the *Step 1 of 2 — add a comment marker to the content* example on `PATCH /v3/projects/{projectId}/articles/{articleId}` (or `PATCH /v3/projects/{projectId}/categories/{categoryId}/content` for a page category) — same `comment_id` (`b7f3c1a0-5e42-4d18-9a6c-2f8091d3e547`), so the two examples are one worked flow: 1. `PATCH` the content so it contains `

The order matters: this endpoint reads the stored content and returns `422` naming the id if the marker is absent, so a comment can never exist without the highlight it annotates. Sending the same `comment_id` twice returns `409` rather than creating a second thread, which makes a retried request safe to repeat.

post.summary: Reply to a comment on a page category.
post.description:
Adds a reply to an existing comment thread on a page category — a single call, with no marker and no
content update involved. Semantics match the article endpoint: a resolved thread returns `409`,
reply creation never overwrites an existing reply, and the per-thread reply limit is enforced.
            
**Access:** requires the `categories.update` permission, the same node-level ACL as the category,
and a resolvable user identity.

### Related endpoints

**Before you call this**
- `GET /v3/projects/{project_id}/categories/{category_id}/comments` — Lists the threads on the page category. Supplies the `comment_id` to reply to.

**See also**
- `PATCH /v3/projects/{project_id}/categories/{category_id}/comments/{comment_id}` — Reopens a resolved thread so it can be replied to again.

Reopens a resolved thread so it can be replied to again.

patch.summary: Resolve, reopen, or edit a comment on a page category.
patch.description:
Updates an existing thread. Send `status` to resolve or reopen it, `comment` to replace its
body, or both. Semantics match the article endpoint: resolving is idempotent, an unreachable transition
is refused with `422` (a thread is `reopened` only after having been `resolved`, and
`open` cannot be set), and the two fields carry different access rules — `status` needs
permission to resolve comments, while editing `comment` is restricted to the thread's author.

### Related endpoints

**Before you call this**
- `GET /v3/projects/{project_id}/categories/{category_id}/comments` — Lists the threads on the page category. Supplies the `comment_id` to update and its current `status`.

**See also**
- `POST /v3/projects/{project_id}/categories/{category_id}/comments/{comment_id}/replies` — Adds a reply instead of editing someone else's body.

parameters.name: comment_id
parameters.description: The identifier of the comment thread to update.

requestBody.description: The status and/or body to apply.

Resolve the thread.summary: Marks the discussion settled. Safe to repeat: a thread that is already resolved is left alone and still returns 200, so a retry after a timeout cannot reopen it.

Reopen a resolved thread.summary: Returns a resolved thread to discussion. Only reachable from `resolved` — reopening a thread that was never resolved is rejected with 422, and `open` cannot be set at all.

Edit the comment body (author only).summary: Replaces the body and its @-mentions. Restricted to the thread's original author whatever their permissions; anyone else gets 403 and should reply instead.

value.comment: Confirmed with security — ninety days is correct.

Edit and resolve in one call.summary: Both fields applied together. Because their access rules differ, a caller who is permitted to resolve but is not the author will be refused — send the two changes separately if that applies.

value.comment: Confirmed with security — ninety days is correct.

parameters.name: filter_to_date

put.description:
Changes only the name users see. The stored object is untouched — `file_url` and
`thumbnail_url` keep their existing values, so every article that already embeds the file
continues to render and no reference needs updating.

so a rename can never change a file's type. Names are unique per project — a collision returns
`422`. Requires `UpdateDrive` permission.

patch.description: Performs a partial update of the project's custom scripts (for the current knowledge base site generation) — only the fields included in the request body are changed; an omitted field is left unchanged, and a field sent as an empty string clears the stored value. The submitted CSS/JavaScript is stored verbatim and injected into the public knowledge base site, so it is intentionally not HTML-sanitized. It is instead checked for gross structural validity — a maximum size, balanced `()`/`[]`/`{}`, and terminated strings, comments and template literals — so malformed code that would break the live site is rejected with `422`. Requires `UpdateCustomCSSAndJS` permission. Read the current values with `GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/custom-scripts`.

Clear JavaScript.summary: Sends an empty string to remove the custom JavaScript while leaving the CSS unchanged.

post.description:
Initiates an asynchronous export task and returns `202 Accepted` with a task ID. Poll
the export status using `GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/exports/{exportId}` until the
task completes. Optionally scope the export to a specific workspace by providing a
`workspaceId` in the request body. If you omit `workspaceId` or send `*`, all
workspaces are exported. An unknown `workspaceId` returns `422`.
Requires `UpdateProjectSettings` permission.
The `format` field selects the export type and is case-insensitive: `json` produces
the JSON export, and `html` (alias `webhelp`) produces the offline HTML (WebHelp)
export. Other values, such as `pdf` or `markdown`, return `422` and no export
task is created.

Export as HTML (offline documentation).summary: Exports the workspace as offline HTML documentation (WebHelp) with an index.html file and a folder for each language.

Export as JSON.summary: Exports the workspace content as JSON files with category and article metadata.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of article summaries within the specified workspace. Pagination is performed in-memory
after fetching all articles, so large datasets may have higher latency. The `pageSize` parameter accepts
a maximum value of `100`. If `langCode` is omitted, articles are returned in the project's default language.
Use `GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/articles/{articleId}` to retrieve full article content.
            
Each summary carries change-detection fields for sync/backup tooling: `status`, `latest_version`,
`public_version`, `modified_at`, and `content_hash`. The hash is the SHA-256 of the latest
version's stored content (prefixed `sha256:`) and changes only when the content itself changes — compare
it against a previously recorded value to skip unchanged articles without downloading them. A `null`
hash means the article has not been saved since hash tracking was introduced; fetch it once to baseline.

newest-archived first. Reuses the SAME M:Document360.Business.Archive.IArchiveBusinessService.GetArchivedItemsAsync(Document360.Core.Models.Documentation.Archive.ArchivedItemsListRequestModel)

post.description: Sends a natural language query to the AI assistive search engine and returns a generated answer based on the project's documentation content. Both `WorkspaceId` and `Query` are required in the request body; a `422` is returned if either is missing or empty. Use `POST /v3/projects/{projectId}/workspaces/ai/feedback` to submit user feedback on the generated response. Content scope. The answer is generated only from content the calling principal may read. The requested workspace must be within the caller's content access (otherwise `404`), and for protected or mixed projects the caller's category, article and language restrictions are applied to the source documents as well, so an answer is never synthesised from denied content. For projects whose protection level is fully public, all published content in the workspace is eligible — it is readable by anyone on the knowledge base site regardless of API permissions.

original_category_id.description: The identifier of the category this item lived under immediately before archiving. Null for a root-level item.

parent_archived.description: True when this row's parent category is itself archived — i.e. this row is a DESCENDANT of another archived item, not an independently restorable one. This endpoint returns every archived item (unlike the Portal's Archive grid, which lists root rows only), so a consumer must check this flag before attempting to RESTORE a row: doing so on a row with this flag set to true is rejected with `409 ARCHIVED_CONTENT_READ_ONLY`. Restore only — permanent delete has no such guard. A row with `parent_archived: true` CAN still be permanently deleted; delete-forever is deliberately not subtree-gated the way restore is. Do not infer anything about delete-forever from this flag.

can_restore.description:
Whether the acting caller HOLDS THE PERMISSION to restore this item — a role/ACL check, wholly
independent of Document360.Customer.API.Models.V3.Archive.ArchivedItemSummaryResponse.ParentArchived. The two can disagree: a row can carry
`can_restore: true` (the caller has the permission) alongside `parent_archived: true`
(the actual restore call is still refused with `409` because the row is a descendant of a
still-archived category). `can_restore` answers "am I allowed to try", not "will this
specific call succeed" — check `parent_archived` too before attempting a restore.

can_delete_forever.description: Whether the acting caller is permitted to permanently delete this item.

ArchivedItemSummaryResponse.description:
One row of a workspace's archive section: an archived article or category language, plus the
acting caller's own restore / delete-forever permission for that row.

category_id.description: The id of the category to move the article to. Combine with `order` to position it in the destination. Retrieve category IDs from `GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/workspaces/{workspaceId}/categories`.

hidden.description: Whether the article should be hidden from readers.

version_number.description: The version number to apply the update to. Defaults to the latest version if omitted. When `auto_fork` is true and this version is published, the update is applied to the newly created draft version, not the original published version.

translation_option.description: The updated translation status of the article.

source.description: The source of the update. Common values: `API`, `import`, `portal`. When omitted, defaults to `API` for Customer API requests.

order.description: The updated 0-based display position within the category (lower = higher in the list).

auto_fork.description: When true and the target version is published, a new draft version is automatically forked and the update (including content and title) is applied to the new draft. When the target version is already a draft, no fork occurs and the update is applied directly. When false (default), updating `content` or `title` on a published version returns a 422 error — both are stored on the article version. Fields that are not version-scoped (`order`, `category_id`, `hidden`, `translation_option`) apply to the article itself and never require a fork. With an API key or API token (M2M), also send `user_id` — the request is rejected with 422 without it.

user_id.description: The identifier of the user making the update. Required when `auto_fork` is true and the request is authenticated with an API key or API token (M2M) without `X-Acting-User-Id` — the user becomes the author of the forked draft version and must have permission to update the article. Optional otherwise. When using a user access token (OAuth), this field is ignored — the user ID is resolved from the token. Retrieve user IDs from `GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/users`.

Required when this item sets `auto_fork` to true and the request is authenticated with an API key or API token (M2M) without `X-Acting-User-Id` — the user becomes the author of the forked draft version. id.description:
Unique identifier of the comment thread, and the value carried by the comment's marker in the content
as `data-comment-id`.


Do not rely on finding it in a `content_mode=raw` response. Raw mode returns the DFM markdown
representation, and a `<mark>` marker does not survive the conversion into it — only the
Editor 3.0 `<span>` form passes through. Use Document360.Customer.API.Models.V3.CommentResponse.CommentedText to learn what a
comment annotates rather than searching the content yourself.

title.description: Optional title/summary of the comment thread.

commented_text.description:
The text in the document that this comment annotates — the content inside its highlight marker — as
plain text.


Read from the document's current content on every request rather than stored with the comment, so it
always reflects what the text says now. A consequence worth knowing: edit the annotated sentence and
this value changes; it is not a record of what the text said when the comment was written.

`null` when the annotated text cannot be determined, which is an ordinary outcome and not an
error — the marker was removed (the thread is orphaned and now annotates nothing), the document is
stored in a form this cannot read, or the comment predates the marker convention. Treat it as
"unknown", and do not assume a comment with `null` here is invalid.


A comment may annotate a selection spanning several paragraphs; those fragments are joined with single
spaces, and runs of whitespace from the document's own markup are collapsed. Long selections are
truncated — see Document360.Customer.API.Models.V3.CommentResponse.CommentedTextTruncated.

commented_text_truncated.description:
Whether Document360.Customer.API.Models.V3.CommentResponse.CommentedText was cut short because the annotated selection exceeded the
response limit. When `true`, the value is a prefix of the real annotated text, not the whole of
it — fetch the document content if the full span matters.

CommentResponse.description:
A single inline comment thread left on an article or category by an author/reviewer, together with its
replies. The `id` matches the `data-comment-id` attribute of the comment's marker in the
content, so a consumer editing the content can re-associate a comment with the exact text it annotates.


Two marker forms exist, and both are valid — which one a document uses depends on the editor that wrote
it: `<mark data-comment-id="…">` for block (Advanced WYSIWYG) content, and
`<span data-comment-id="…" class="d360-comment …">` for Editor 3.0. Match on the attribute
rather than on the element name.

workspace_id.description: Unique identifier of the workspace to import the API reference into.

publish_articles.description: Whether to automatically publish the generated API reference articles after import.

user_id.description:
User ID that performs the publish. Required ONLY when `publish_articles` is `true` and the
request is authenticated with an API token (M2M), because such a credential carries no user identity
and publishing must be attributed to a real user. Ignored when a user access token is used - the user
is taken from the token. Not needed at all when `publish_articles` is `false`.
Retrieve user IDs from `GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/users`.

force_import.description: Import the specification even when it produces validation findings. Defaults to `false` (WI 340551): the caller is told what the import would do and re-submits with `force_import: true` to go ahead. This default changed. It was `true`, matching the V1/V2 `ForceImport` contract. Under `true` a resync deleted endpoints and said nothing about it, because the deletion report was computed only on the strict path — so on V3, where this initialised to `true`, a destructive resync was always silent. The gate is broader than deletions. Under `false` the request is refused if the spec yields ANY error or warning, or if `servers` is absent, so a spec that parses perfectly can still be refused. That is the cost of the change and it is deliberate: a refusal is recoverable in one call, a silent deletion is not.

ImportApiReferenceRequest.description: Request to import an API reference specification (OpenAPI/Swagger) into the project.

id.description: Unique identifier of the import task. Use this to poll for import status.

status.description: Terminal status of the import operation. Null while the operation is still running. Import and resync are accepted with `202` and processed in the background (WI 340551), so there is no outcome to report at that point — read Document360.Customer.API.Models.V3.ImportApiReferenceResponse.OperationStatus instead, and poll the `Operation-Location` header for the final result. Nullable on purpose: a non-nullable enum would default to `Success` and report an outcome that has not happened.

operation_id.description:
Id of the background operation processing this request (WI 340551). Poll it at
`GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/operations/{operationId}`, or follow the
`Operation-Location` response header.

operation_status.description:
Lifecycle status of that operation, in the same vocabulary the operations endpoint uses —
so the value here is the value you will keep seeing while polling.

deleted_endpoints.description:
Endpoints that existed in the previous specification, are absent from this one, and whose
generated articles were therefore removed.
            


Populated on a RESYNC only — a first import has nothing to delete. Omitted when nothing was
removed, so a caller can treat its presence as the signal.


Added by WI 340551. Before it, a resync run with `force_import=true` — which was this
API's default until the same work item changed it to `false` — removed endpoint
articles and reported nothing about it. Under the current `false` default the
destructive run is refused instead, and this field reports what it WOULD remove. When you
re-submit with `force_import: true` to confirm, this field is a report of what
happened, NOT a prompt: by the time you read it the deletion has already been applied.
Recoverability depends on the project's recycle-bin entitlement.

user_id.description:
User ID that performs the publish. Required ONLY when `publish_articles` is `true` and the
request is authenticated with an API token (M2M), because such a credential carries no user identity
and publishing must be attributed to a real user. Ignored when a user access token is used - the user
is taken from the token. Not needed at all when `publish_articles` is `false`.
Retrieve user IDs from `GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/users`.

force_import.description:
Resync even when the refreshed specification produces validation findings. Defaults to
`false` (WI 340551).


This matters most on resync, which is the destructive operation: a spec that no longer
describes an endpoint causes that endpoint's article to be deleted and recreated with a new
id. Under the old `true` default that happened without the caller being told. Now the
response carries `deleted_endpoints` and the caller re-submits with
`force_import: true` to confirm.


See Document360.Customer.API.Models.V3.ImportApiReferenceRequest.ForceImport — the same gate also refuses on any
error or warning, not only on deletions.

ResyncApiReferenceRequest.description:
Request to resync an existing API reference with a fresh OpenAPI/Swagger spec. Re-runs the
import pipeline against the existing API reference record, replacing its spec source. The
diff is reflected as updates to the auto-generated articles — additions, modifications, and
removals of operations all flow through. Use after the underlying API has shipped a new
version of its spec. The refreshed spec is taken from either `url` or `content`.

UnpublishRequest.description: Request to unpublish an article or category version, reverting it to draft.

title.description: The updated title of the article.

content.description: The updated body content of the article. Markdown for markdown articles; HTML for block or wysiwyg articles. For HTML content the server also derives and stores a markdown representation automatically.
content.example: # Introduction\nThis updated guide walks you through configuring SSO.

category_id.description: The id of the category to move the article to. Combine with `order` to position it in the destination. Retrieve category IDs from `GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/workspaces/{workspaceId}/categories`.

hidden.description: Whether the article should be hidden from readers.

version_number.description: The version number to apply the update to. Defaults to the latest version if omitted. When `auto_fork` is true and this version is published, the update is applied to the newly created draft version, not the original published version.

translation_option.description: The updated translation status of the article.

source.description: The source of the update. Common values: `API`, `import`, `portal`. When omitted, defaults to `API` for Customer API requests.

order.description: The updated 0-based display position within the category (lower = higher in the list).

auto_fork.description: When true and the target version is published, a new draft version is automatically forked and the update (including content and title) is applied to the new draft. When the target version is already a draft, no fork occurs and the update is applied directly. When false (default), updating `content` or `title` on a published version returns a 422 error — both are stored on the article version. Fields that are not version-scoped (`order`, `category_id`, `hidden`, `translation_option`) apply to the article itself and never require a fork. With an API key or API token (M2M), also send `user_id` — the request is rejected with 422 without it.

user_id.description: The identifier of the user making the update. Required when `auto_fork` is true and the request is authenticated with an API key or API token (M2M) without `X-Acting-User-Id` — the user becomes the author of the forked draft version and must have permission to update the article. Optional otherwise. When using a user access token (OAuth), this field is ignored — the user ID is resolved from the token. Retrieve user IDs from `GET /v3/projects/{projectId}/users`.

ApiKey.description: API key for machine-to-machine integrations, webhooks, and CI/CD (recommended). This is a static, pre-shared secret - treat it as an opaque string and do not parse it; it is an API key, not an OAuth 2.0 access token. Create one in the portal under **Settings > Knowledge base portal > API keys** using the **Create API key** button - this is a different credential from the V1/V2 *API token*, which lives on its own screen and will not authenticate a V3 request. The plaintext key (format `d360_sk_...`) is shown only once, at creation. Send it in the `X-API-Key` header: `X-API-Key: d360_sk_...`. Each key carries a fixed portal role, content role, and content-access scope, supports an optional expiry, and can be disabled or deleted at any time from the portal.
ApiKey.name: X-API-Key

Bearer.description: All V3 endpoints require a Bearer token. Generate tokens in the Document360 portal under **Settings > API Tokens**. Tokens are project-scoped, require the `customerApi` scope, and do not expire by default. Tokens can be revoked at any time from the portal. Include the token in every request: `Authorization: Bearer <your-token>`. Alternatively, use the Authorize button below to sign in via OAuth2 Authorization Code flow with PKCE.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description: List and manage knowledge base projects. Export and import project documentation, and manage project-level site customization such as custom CSS and JavaScript.

tags.name: Projects > Import & export
tags.description: Start a project export or import and poll the resulting background operation for completion.

tags.name: Workspaces
tags.description: Manage workspaces and access workspace-scoped categories and articles.

tags.name: Workspaces > AI
tags.description: Query the workspace with Eddy AI and submit feedback on AI answers.

tags.name: Articles
tags.description: Create, read, update, and delete knowledge base articles and their settings, including bulk operations.

tags.name: Articles > Publishing & workflow
tags.description: Publish and unpublish articles (single and bulk) and update the article workflow status.

tags.name: Articles > Versions
tags.description: List, fork, and delete article versions.

tags.name: Articles > Attachments
tags.description: Manage the files attached to an article — list, upload, and delete article attachments.

tags.name: Articles > Content drafts
tags.description: (Internal) Stage AI-generated article content with an Accept/Reject review lifecycle — used by Eddy Copilot to preview content before committing to the live article body.

tags.name: Articles > Labels
tags.description: Read and set the labels associated with an article.

tags.name: Articles > Comments
tags.description: Read and create the comment threads authors and reviewers leave on an article's content, and reply to them. Each comment id matches the `data-comment-id` attribute of the corresponding marker in the raw article content, so adding a text-anchored comment takes two calls: update the content with the marker, then create the thread with the same id.

tags.name: Categories
tags.description: Manage the category hierarchy that organizes articles. Create, update, and delete categories and their settings, including bulk operations.

tags.name: Categories > Page category
tags.description: Read and update the content body of page-type categories, including bulk content updates.

tags.name: Categories > Publishing & workflow
tags.description: Publish and unpublish categories (single and bulk) and update the category workflow status.

tags.name: Categories > Versions
tags.description: List, fork, and delete category versions.

tags.name: Categories > Labels
tags.description: Read and set the labels associated with a category.

tags.name: Categories > Comments
tags.description: Read and create the comment threads authors and reviewers leave on a page category's content, and reply to them. Only page-type categories carry content, so other category types return `404`. Adding a text-anchored comment takes two calls: update the content with the marker, then create the thread with the same id.

tags.name: ArticleTemplates
tags.description: Manage reusable article templates — per-language article skeletons that authors and AI tools (such as Eddy Copilot) can apply when starting a new article.

tags.name: Content reuse > Glossaries
tags.description: Manage glossary entries — terminology definitions referenced inside articles via merge codes (`{{glossary.name}}`) and rendered as tooltips on the public KB.

tags.name: Content reuse > Snippets
tags.description: Manage reusable snippets — markdown or WYSIWYG content fragments referenced across articles via merge codes (`{{snippet.name}}`).

tags.name: Content reuse > Variables
tags.description: Manage reusable variables — short text values referenced across articles via merge codes (`{{variable.name}}`).

tags.name: AiWriterStyleGuides
tags.description: Retrieve AI writer style guides configured for the project — voice / tone instructions Eddy Copilot follows when generating article content. Used to let users pick a style before kicking off generation.

tags.name: RedirectRules
tags.description: Manage article-redirection rules — 301/302 redirects from old article URLs to new locations after renames or restructures.

tags.name: Tags
tags.description: Manage tags — labels used to classify articles, categories, and files for filtering and discovery.

tags.name: Labels
tags.description: Manage labels shown on the article list and category tree. (Associating labels with a specific article or category lives under Articles and Categories.)

tags.name: CustomFields
tags.description: Retrieve the custom field definitions configured for the project. Custom field values are read and written through the article and category settings endpoints.

tags.name: ApiReferences
tags.description: Import, resync, and publish OpenAPI/Swagger specifications for API reference documentation.

tags.name: ApiReferences > Logs
tags.description: Monitor API reference import logs and inspect individual log entries.

tags.name: Drive
tags.description: Search Drive and retrieve files associated with an article, and track Drive background tasks.

tags.name: Drive > Folders
tags.description: Create, read, update, and delete Drive folders.

tags.name: Drive > Files
tags.description: Upload, copy, move, delete, and tag Drive files.

tags.name: Drive > Image drafts
tags.description: (Internal) Stage uploaded or AI-generated images (committed to Drive and associated with a staged article draft) — used by Eddy Copilot.

tags.name: Readers
tags.description: Manage reader accounts, invitations, and access scopes for private documentation.

tags.name: Readers > Groups
tags.description: Create, read, update, and delete reader groups.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: Manage users, their portal and content roles, and consolidated (effective) permissions within a project.

tags.name: Users > Groups
tags.description: Manage user groups, their portal role, and consolidated (effective) group permissions.

tags.name: Roles
tags.description: Create, read, update, and delete portal and content roles, list the users assigned to a role, and retrieve the permission dependency matrix.

tags.name: ContentAccess
tags.description: Manage per-node content-access permissions — grant, allow, deny, and inheritance overrides for users and groups against specific versions, languages, categories, or articles, plus version/language site protection.

tags.name: ContentAccess > Eligibility
tags.description: List the readers and groups eligible to be granted content access.

tags.name: Languages
tags.description: Retrieve configured languages for a workspace.

tags.name: Translations
tags.description: Query translation status of articles across languages.

tags.name: Operations
tags.description: Track asynchronous operations — long-running tasks (bulk updates, merges, exports) accepted with `202 Accepted` and an `Operation-Location` header. Poll until the operation reaches a terminal status, honouring the `Retry-After` header.

tags.name: Analytics > Articles

tags.name: Analytics > Search
tags.description: View search usage metrics including top keywords, no-result queries, and bounced searches.

tags.name: Analytics > AI search
tags.description: View AI-powered search metrics including usage trends, most-referenced articles, and trending topics.

tags.name: Analytics > Feedback
